finding: A Mac sample of the 1d build (frozen 834fc05d, 20 s during gameplay; scratchpad rt1d-mac-sample.txt) put 467 of 2,347 busy main-thread samples (20%) in kevent_id under RenderExecutor.flush <- performFront <- replay: every text step flushed the render queue, so a batch that draws HUD text waited for its queued pixel work.
change: OriginalMacDisplayBackend: the DC steps (acquire, mode, background, colour, release) change the text DC alone and no longer flush. TextOutA (drawText) is split into textPlan (main thread: storage check, the host's glyph mask, the DC's opacity and colours as values), textPixels (static) and bounds. Without pipelining it flushes and runs the old order (pixels, frontTarget, present). Pipelining: a released surface flushes and throws before drawing; empty bounds queue the pixels; frontTarget (rectangle and geometry only) is checked before queuing and a failure flushes, draws and rethrows; then the fill/copy pipeline (a failed present check flushes, draws, rethrows) and the closure draws and delivers the crop. textCell is nonisolated.

review: independent read-only review: no correctness issues. Main-thread pixel readers all flush; the DC steps touch no pixels and the DC state is copied into the plan; error paths equivalent (frontTarget reads no pixels, host call order unchanged); the closure holds Storage and values; serial order kept; the non-pipelined path is the old code.
